newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Egis to invest HUF 5bln to 6bln in '97-CEO.
newsitem.headline: Egis to invest HUF 5bln to 6bln in '97-CEO.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Rt plans to spend five billion to six billion forints this year on investment, R&D and marketing, the company's CEO told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We have to keep up with in an increasingly competitive environment," Egis CEO Istvan Orban said.
He added that the high investment rate explains the size of the dividend on the 1996 earnings.
The company's annual general meeting on Tuesday approved an eight percent or 80 forints per share dividend on the 1996 results, the same as the 1995 dividend.
In 1996 the company posted after-tax profit of 5.6 billion forints on net sales of 24.69 billion forints.
Orban said they aim for a "sustainable growth" this year.
Company officials said in February that the company plans to increase its sales to around 30 billion forints in 1997 and plans to post a pre-tax profit of 6.3 billion.
Orban said the company regarded east Europe as its main export market but within that was especially focusing on Russia. "It is a huge, unsaturated market," he said.
He said Poland also played a special role in the company's export plans as they had a joint production facility there with Egis's majority owner and strategic partner, France's Servier S.A.
Servier holds a 50.91 percent stake in Egis, foreign institutional investors 44.72 percent while the rest is held by Hungarian institutional and private investors.
Orban added that Egis was also increasing its presence in western Europe, a move that would be of advantage in its core east European exort market.
"Western European standards will become an important competition factor in east Europe as well," he said.
Another company official said Egis's new packaging line has been completed and will shortly come on line.
"This will allow us to appear on every market," Laszlo Marosffy, Egis's financial vice-president, told shareholders.
The company was active in the UK, Germany and, through Servier, in France as well, Orban said.
He said that last year the company reduced its worforce by 202 to 2,722 people, increasing the percentage of highly-qualified personnel as a result.
He added that increasing the educational level of the employees was a costly but necessary step.
Orban said the company was not planning any changes in its proven strategy.
"We don't need to change our strategy," he said. "Egis has been a drugs-only operation for years and we were concentrating on the markets where we can be competitive".
